section_summary.extract_value: This abstract reports a single 7-night diary study in which 92 female undergraduates reported daily on social interactions, self-compassion, body image, eating, and affect. Results indicate that on days when women were less self-compassionate, frequent interactions with body-focused others were linked to worse body image, negative affect, and poorer eating-related outcomes, whereas higher-than-usual self-compassion buffered or reversed these relations.
section_summary.evidence_source: "We examined whether a woman's level of self-compassion on a given day (within-persons) and over a week (between-persons)influenced her eating, body image, and affect... For seven nights, 92 female undergraduates reported on their daily social interactions, self-compassion, body image, eating, and affect. On days when women were less self-compassionate than usual, frequent interactions with body-focused others were associated with more body image concerns and negative affect, and less body appreciation and intuitive eating."
